newsitem.title: USA: Crude prices flounder slightly, Sept grades sloppy.
newsitem.headline: Crude prices flounder slightly, Sept grades sloppy.

text.p: September crude grades started Monday with a whimper, working steadily against a slumping outright crude price.
Traders said action for new September business failed to jolt differentials, though the West Texas Sour/Midland market firmed slightly from Friday.

Outright September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood 5-10 cents weaker late on Monday, talked in a range from $19.75-85 a barrel. September/October spreads, or rolls, were from 7-9 cents in favor of October.
Trades saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at 20 cents over the benchmark, with talked ranges at 20-23 cents over September WTI/Cushing.

West Texas Sour/Midland was heard sold at $1.60 and $1.45 under September WTI, with the later deal reflecting a firming market. Eugene Island talked at $1.50-30 below the WTI, with little action materializing late.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus was at $1.93-$2.00, with deals done at $1.92.
Futures prices saw weakness in the crude market, while gasoline values spiked higher briefly on news of a refinery problem at the Venezuelan Punta Cardon facility.

Iraq also made the news Monday, after envoy to the United Nations Nizar Hamdoon said annexes to the main body of Baghdad'd aid distribution plan were delivered to the U.N. in New York. Senior U.N. officials and Western diplomats still expect U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to approve the plan before the end of the week, putting renewed oil sales one step closer to reality.
